confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches of aggregator and cost-of-living summaries. The figures are in AUD, crowd-sourced, and mostly dated mid-2026. I converted them at about 0.672 USD per AUD. Cappuccino was about AUD 5 to 5.7. A 0.5 L draught beer was about AUD 10 to 13.3, and I used a standard restaurant serving of about AUD 12.5. An inexpensive meal was about AUD 25.5. A mid-range meal for two was about AUD 123, and I used about AUD 125. Cocktail prices ranged from about AUD 18 to 28, averaging about AUD 22. A glass of house wine was about AUD 12 to 16, and I used about AUD 13.5. The sources disagree somewhat, and some cocktail and wine figures come from generated summary pages, so drinks are less certain than coffee and meals. The beer serving size is ambiguous because schooners, pints and 0.5 L pours are all common. I did not search for accommodation prices. Those four anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Melbourne for July, which is the winter low-to-shoulder season, and they are the least certain. For context, July 2026 is already in the past, while the FX figure is the latest RBA observation available on the generation date. The FX value, 0.6720 USD per AUD at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026, comes from a web-search result that cites the RBA exchange-rates page. I did not open the page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Melbourne-specific aggregator data for food and drink. For accommodation, I estimated from Melbourne's position as a high-cost Australian capital, slightly below Sydney, with winter demand somewhat lower than in summer.
